text.p: Shares in rail infrastructure group Railtrack Plc leapt to an all-time high on Wednesday, but were still undervalued, according to analysts.
The shares jumped 30-1/2p to 715-1/2p after easing slightly from an intraday peak of 719p. Volume was 2.8 million shares.
"The stock seems to be struggling a bit around the 715-720p level," said one market-maker. "But the shares are still undervalued because of regulation worries running up to the budget."
One leading industry analyst said he would recommend buying the shares up to a value of 8.00 stg.
"The company came out of the budget reasonably well," the analyst said. "The worry was overdone and now they're catching up."
Market-makers said buying interest had resurfaced since the budget but they dismissed market talk that vague bid rumours were helping to spark interest.

Traders said a Times newspaper report that said Chancellor Gordon Brown had effectively engineered a property boom in the UK by encouraging investment funds into commercial property rather than equities was helping sentiment.
A continuing flight to safety stocks relying on domestic income and protected from a soaring currency was also cited as helping the shares.
